general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **United States/China:** Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping commenced a high-stakes summit in Beijing on Thursday, May 14, to address critical issues including the ongoing war in Iran, global trade imbalances, competition in artificial intelligence and semiconductor exports, and the sensitive issue of Taiwan. This meeting is crucial for de-escalating geopolitical tensions and shaping future economic cooperation and technological leadership between the world's two largest economies.

• **Middle East/Global Economy:** Geopolitical tensions continue to escalate near the Strait of Hormuz, with the ongoing US-Iran conflict driving Brent crude prices above $100 per barrel and causing concerns about fuel inflation worldwide. This sustained instability in a critical global energy choke point is significantly impacting international supply chains and contributing to inflationary pressures across various economies.

• **United States Economy:** US headline inflation rose to 3.8% year-over-year in April 2026, exceeding forecasts, largely due to a significant oil shock stemming from the Middle East conflict. This inflationary surge is eroding real wages for American families and is shifting market expectations towards potential Federal Reserve interest rate hikes in early 2027.

• **Japan/Science & Technology:** Scientists in Japan have achieved a breakthrough by developing a new method to instantly detect quantum "W states," a critical step forward for quantum technology. This advancement has the potential to revolutionize quantum communication, enable faster teleportation-like technologies, and pave the way for more powerful next-generation quantum computing systems.

Why it matters: Persistent geopolitical conflicts and their economic repercussions are driving global inflationary pressures and challenging financial stability, even as rapid advancements in key technologies like quantum computing continue to reshape future industrial and communication landscapes.

ai_productivity.title: ⚡ AI & Productivity
ai_productivity.content:
• **OpenAI:** GPT-5.5 Instant shipped as the default model in ChatGPT, offering improved accuracy and speed, specifically reducing hallucinations in sensitive domains like law, medicine, and finance. This means users receive more reliable and faster responses for critical inquiries, minimizing the need for extensive manual verification.

• **Perplexity:** Launched Personal Computer for Mac, securely connecting local files and applications to Perplexity's Computer agent, and integrated Computer into Microsoft Teams. This allows AI agents to directly leverage local desktop context and team communications, significantly streamlining multi-application and collaborative workflows.

• **Figma:** Released Custom Skills in Make, enabling designers to define reusable design conventions, workflows, and sample data as markdown files callable via slash commands. This empowers design teams to maintain consistent patterns and data usage across projects with fewer prompts, accelerating prototyping and design system adherence.

• **Notion:** Launched its Developer Platform, including an External Agents API, database sync capabilities, and a Notion CLI. This allows developers to integrate Notion deeply with other data sources and custom AI agents, transforming Notion into a central orchestration layer for complex, automated workflows.

• **Cursor:** Shipped Development Environments for Cloud Agents, providing tools to configure multi-repository agent environments with "configuration as code" and enabling parallel execution of development plans. This allows engineering teams to deploy and manage AI agents in controlled environments, speeding up end-to-end coding tasks by multitasking on independent steps.

Why it matters: The focus of recent AI advancements is shifting towards deeply integrated, autonomous agents and developer platforms that enable AI to operate within existing workflows and local environments, rather than as standalone chat interfaces.

eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **Amendments to the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689):** Previously, obligations for high-risk Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems were set to become effective on August 2, 2026. Following a political agreement on May 7, 2026, compliance deadlines are now deferred: for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III (e.g., biometrics, critical infrastructure, employment, education, law enforcement), the new compliance deadline is December 2, 2027. For AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery, toys, lifts), the deadline is August 2, 2028. Additionally, a new prohibition on AI systems generating non-consensual sexually explicit or intimate content (such as "nudifier" applications) applies from December 2, 2026. Transparency obligations for chatbots will take effect in August 2026, and providers of generative AI must ensure AI-generated content is identifiable (watermarked) by December 2, 2026, with a shorter grace period for systems placed on the market before August 2, 2026. Simplified technical documentation requirements are also extended from small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to small mid-cap companies. This significantly extends the compliance runway for businesses developing or deploying high-risk AI systems in the EU and introduces new ethical safeguards.

• **European Commission Guidance on Money Market Funds (MMFs) Framework:** Previously, EU Money Market Funds adhered to existing regulatory minima for liquidity reserves, under a framework in application since 2018. On May 11-12, 2026, the European Commission adopted updated guidance in the form of Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) to provide further clarity and enhance resilience. New benchmarks specify appropriate weekly liquidity levels as 40% for stable net asset value MMFs and 20% for variable net asset value MMFs, based on extensive data analysis. This guidance aims to help MMF managers and competent authorities identify situations warranting closer scrutiny and improve risk management, contributing to financial stability.

• **New Technology Transfer Block Exemption Regulation (TTBER) and Guidelines:** Previously, technology licensing agreements were assessed under the 2014 TTBER and its accompanying Guidelines. The new TTBER and Guidelines, adopted on April 16, 2026, and taking effect on May 1, 2026, revise this framework. Key changes include clarified market share thresholds, where technologies without generated sales are deemed to have 0% market share for calculation purposes, and an extended grace period for exceeding market share thresholds from two to three years. New guidance is also provided for data licensing, applying TTBER principles by analogy for copyright- or sui generis-protected databases, with other forms requiring case-by-case assessment. Guidance on technology pools is tightened, requiring disclosure of individual rights, the methodology for assessing their essentiality, and preventing licensees from being charged more than once for the same technology rights ("double dipping"). This provides greater legal certainty and updated rules for businesses engaged in technology licensing and intellectual property within the EU, impacting competitive strategies.

• **Regulation on the Protection of Adults in Cross-Border Situations (Provisional Agreement):** Previously, adults needing protection or support (e.g., due to disability or health-related limitations) and their representatives often faced legal complexities and administrative burdens when their personal, legal, medical, or financial affairs crossed EU national borders. A provisional agreement was reached on May 12, 2026, between the European Parliament and the Council of the EU on a new Regulation. This introduces EU-wide rules to establish which court has jurisdiction, what law is applicable, and how protection measures or powers of representation established in one Member State are recognized in another, along with improved cooperation among authorities. It also introduces a European Certificate of Support and Representation, simplifying the process for representatives to prove their powers in other Member States. The legislation will enter into force 20 days after its publication in the Official Journal, with measures progressively applying from 24 months thereafter. This safeguards the autonomy and rights of vulnerable adults, including Portuguese citizens, who move or reside across EU Member States, reducing legal uncertainty and administrative hurdles.

Why it matters: The political agreement on amendments to the AI Act is the most significant EU-level change this week, providing crucial clarity and extended deadlines for businesses navigating the EU's pioneering AI regulatory framework, while also addressing urgent ethical concerns.

us_policy.title: 🇺🇸 United States Policy
us_policy.content:
• **"Build More Hydro" Bill Enacted:** President Donald J. Trump signed S.1020 into law on May 12, 2026, which permits the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to grant six-year extensions for hydropower projects initially licensed before 2020. This action is expected to accelerate the development and expansion of American energy production by reducing regulatory hurdles for existing hydropower facilities.

• **Federal Reserve Terminates Bank Enforcement Actions:** On May 12, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board announced the termination of long-running enforcement actions, effective May 6, 2026, against F & M Holding Company, Inc., and Thread Bancorp, Inc. Previously, both institutions were subject to written agreements, which are common forms of bank regulatory actions; now, these formal supervisory matters are closed. This signals a positive regulatory shift for the involved institutions, potentially improving their operational flexibility and market perception.

• **Treasury Department Directs Banks on Iranian Money Laundering:** On May 12, 2026, the Treasury Department advised U.S. banks and financial institutions to increase monitoring for suspected Iranian money laundering networks that aim to smuggle sanctioned oil through shell companies and crypto networks. This action enhances the enforcement of existing sanctions by effectively deputizing the financial system to help disrupt Iran's sanctions-evasion infrastructure.

• **DOJ Settlement for Evaded Customs Duties:** The Department of Justice announced on May 13, 2026, that Perfectus Aluminum Inc. and related companies agreed to pay $549.5 million to resolve False Claims Act allegations concerning evaded customs duties on imported aluminum products. Previously, these companies allegedly evaded duties, harming American manufacturers; now, they face a substantial financial penalty and accountability for illegal trade practices. This settlement reinforces the government's commitment to combating trade fraud and protecting domestic industries.

• **FTC Settlement with Shutterstock over Subscription Practices:** On May 13, 2026, the Federal Trade Commission announced a settlement requiring Shutterstock Inc. to pay $35 million to resolve allegations of illegal subscription and cancellation practices. Previously, Shutterstock allegedly engaged in unfair and deceptive practices, including charging consumers without informed consent and making cancellations difficult; now, the company must pay a significant fine and implement changes to its business practices. This enforcement action protects consumers from deceptive online subscription models and promotes fair competition in digital markets.

Why it matters: The U.S. government has prioritized a series of targeted enforcement actions and the enactment of legislation designed to bolster domestic energy production, strengthen financial regulatory compliance, and combat illicit trade and deceptive consumer practices, reflecting a clear focus on economic security and market integrity this week.

portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
•   **Pacote de Medidas Fiscais para a Habitação:** O Presidente da República promulgou em 12 de maio de 2026 um decreto-lei que introduz um conjunto de medidas de desagravamento fiscal para estimular a oferta de habitação para venda e arrendamento, com entrada em vigor prevista após a publicação em Diário da República. Anteriormente, o IVA sobre a construção era geralmente de 23%; agora é reduzido para 6% para imóveis destinados ao arrendamento com rendas até 2.300 euros mensais ou à venda a um preço considerado moderado (até aproximadamente 648.000 euros). A taxa autónoma de IRS sobre rendimentos prediais para rendas moderadas é reduzida de 25% para 10%. Adicionalmente, é estabelecida a exclusão de tributação de mais-valias em IRS na venda de habitação própria se o valor for reinvestido em imóveis para arrendamento, e a taxa de IMT para a aquisição de habitação por não residentes é fixada em 7,5%, sem isenções ou reduções. O pacote também prevê um regime de restituição parcial do IVA para pessoas singulares que realizem obras em habitação própria e permanente. O impacto prático é um incentivo significativo para investidores no setor imobiliário e proprietários, visando aumentar a oferta de habitação a preços mais acessíveis e beneficiar indiretamente os cidadãos na procura de casa. [Executive Digest; ECO; Contas Poupança]

•   **Alteração à Lei da Nacionalidade:** Promulgada em 3 de maio de 2026, esta lei endurece as regras para a aquisição da nacionalidade portuguesa, com as alterações a entrarem em vigor em 2026. Anteriormente, o requisito de residência legal para a nacionalidade era de cinco anos; com a nova lei, o prazo mínimo para os requerentes poderem pedir a nacionalidade portuguesa é aumentado para dez anos. Para filhos de imigrantes nascidos em Portugal, a lei anterior permitia a aquisição da nacionalidade sob certas condições; agora, exige que os pais sejam residentes legais há pelo menos cinco anos para que a criança tenha esse direito. O impacto prático é que o processo de obtenção da nacionalidade portuguesa se torna mais longo e exigente para muitos imigrantes, afetando diretamente a sua integração e os seus direitos no país. [Poder360; The Portugal News; YouTube]

•   **Regulação da Contratação de Médicos no SNS e Incentivos para Urgências:** O Conselho de Ministros aprovou em 7 de maio de 2026 um decreto-lei que regula a contratação de médicos em regime de prestação de serviços no Serviço Nacional de Saúde (SNS) e um regime excecional de incentivos remuneratórios para os médicos em serviço de urgência. Anteriormente, a contratação de serviços médicos era menos regulamentada, levando a situações de precarização e desvirtuamento dos serviços de urgência. A nova legislação estabelece que o recurso a prestação de serviços deve ser excecional e complementar aos vínculos públicos, privilegiando médicos especialistas e introduzindo regras de incompatibilidade para evitar a substituição de vínculos permanentes por prestações mais onerosas. O impacto prático é esperado na melhoria da qualidade e estabilidade das equipas médicas no SNS, nomeadamente nos serviços de urgência, o que poderá resultar num melhor acesso e qualidade dos cuidados de saúde para os cidadãos. [Comunicado do Conselho de Ministros; Cister FM; gov.pt]

•   **Horário de Funcionamento e Escalas de Farmácias:** A Portaria n.º 209/2026/1, publicada em Diário da República em 7 de maio de 2026, com entrada em vigor 30 dias após a sua publicação (6 de junho de 2026), altera o regime de horários de funcionamento das farmácias de oficina e as escalas de turnos. A mudança concreta é que, a partir da hora de encerramento normal, as farmácias em assistência farmacêutica podem impedir o acesso do público ao interior, desde que disponham de um postigo de atendimento que permita a dispensa ao público. O impacto prático é uma maior flexibilidade operacional para as farmácias em regime de turno, ao mesmo tempo que garante a continuidade do acesso a medicamentos e produtos farmacêuticos para os cidadãos fora do horário normal de funcionamento. [Diário da República; Tribunal da Relação de Coimbra]

Why it matters: O pacote de medidas fiscais para a habitação e a alteração da Lei da Nacionalidade representam as mudanças mais significativas, impactando diretamente os custos de habitação para cidadãos e empresas, e alterando drasticamente o caminho para a cidadania portuguesa para imigrantes e seus descendentes.
